concepts.label: law of demand and law of supply
quotes: The law of demand says that, other things being equal, when the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls.
The law of supply says that when the price of a good rises, the quantity supplied rises

concepts.label: market equilibrium
quotes: The market equilibrium is the price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied.
At this price there is no pressure for the price to change.

concepts.label: shortage and surplus
quotes: If the price is set below equilibrium, buyers want more than sellers offer, which creates a shortage.
If the price is set above equilibrium, sellers offer more than buyers want, which creates a surplus.

concepts.label: price changes move along demand curve
quotes: A change in price moves the market along the demand curve.
A change in anything else that affects buyers shifts the whole curve.

concepts.label: demand shifters
quotes: These notes list three demand shifters: income, consumer preferences and the prices of related goods.

concepts.label: substitutes and complements
quotes: Substitutes are goods used in place of each other, such as tea and coffee: when coffee becomes more expensive, demand for tea rises.
Complements are goods used together, such as printers and ink cartridges: when printers become cheaper, demand for ink cartridges rises.

concepts.label: price ceiling and price floor
quotes: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price, such as rent control; if it is set below equilibrium, it causes a shortage.
A price floor is a legal minimum price, such as a minimum wage; if it is set above equilibrium, it causes a surplus.

concepts.label: prices as signals
quotes: A rising price tells producers to make more and tells buyers to look for alternatives
